Edward Albee’s 1962 marital warfare masterpiece has been magnificently revived by James Macdonald, exchanging blousy melodrama for taut, psychologically plausible theatre.

cn.t: Staunton and Hill deliver fierce, powerhouse performances in this scorching revival of Albee's masterpiece, though some find the three-hour marital slugfest exhausting and overly bleak. Critics largely praise the production's psychological intensity.
